key_insight: PoM (Polynomial Mixer) replaces self-attention with a learned polynomial aggregation that compresses token context into a compact representation and lets each token retrieve contextual information in linear time, preserving transformer expressivity.
problem_solved: Reduces the quadratic time and memory cost of self-attention for long sequences while maintaining the theoretical ability to approximate sequence-to-sequence mappings.
method: Learn a polynomial function that aggregates N input tokens into a compact fixed-size representation (linear-time aggregation).
Provide a token-wise retrieval mechanism where each token queries the polynomial embedding to obtain contextualized features.
Prove the contextual mapping property (universality) and demonstrate PoM as a drop-in replacement in transformer layers.
impact: Enables scalable transformers for long sequences with substantially lower compute and memory overhead while retaining theoretical expressiveness—useful for practitioners working on long-context language, vision, or multimodal models.
visual_elements: Side-by-side schematic: standard self-attention (O(N^2)) vs PoM pipeline (polynomial aggregation + retrieval, O(N)).
Complexity chart: compute and memory vs sequence length comparing attention and PoM (log-log or linear plot).
Diagram of polynomial aggregation: tokens → learned polynomial encoder → compact representation → per-token retrieval.
Proof intuition panel: simple illustration showing contextual mapping/universality (toy input → reconstructed outputs) to convey theoretical guarantee.
paper_title: PoM: A Linear-Time Replacement for Attention with the Polynomial Mixer
paper_authors: David Picard, Nicolas Dufour, Lucas Degeorge, Arijit Ghosh, Davide Allegro
